hints.title: Units Digit Arithmetic
hints.text: If a set of size s has elements each ending in k, the sum must have units digit (s * k) % 10.

hints.title: Size Bound up to 10
hints.text: Because units digits repeat every 10 multiples, we only need to test sizes s from 1 to 10.

hints.title: Feasibility Condition
hints.text: Size s is valid if s * k <= num and (num - s * k) % 10 == 0. Return the smallest valid s.

hints.title: Units Digit Modular Size Implementation

complexity.notes: Testing at most 10 integer sizes takes constant time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full knapsack DP over numbers takes unnecessary linear or pseudo-polynomial memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate proves that checking sizes 1 through 10 is necessary and sufficient by modular arithmetic.
